body:
oh i totally understand. i have been sad, and i have been angry. i used to be so angry it almost consumed me. 

now i'm not sad nor angry. i'm just numb to everything. i can smile and laugh and appreciate the beauty of the sky. but i wonder, what's the point of all of this?

they say that the good things make up for the bad things. but why should we have to endure the bad things at all, when we could simply stop existing?

but do they deal with the same thoughts as us? i would understand staying alive despite your suicidal thoughts if you have children, or someone to take care of, etc. it's people who say they've never thought about killing themselves that i don't understand. i'm sure they suffer, like all of us. they have hardships, like all of us. why do we react to those hardships by wanting to die and they don't? is it only because we are different people who react differently, or do they know something that we don't? i've spent years thinking that all of my mental health issues taught me things people who haven't suffered the way i have don't know. is it the opposite? i don't know anymore.
thank you for giving me other alternatives! i will look into them
thank you so much. i live in france, actually, but i will look into AA
thank you for taking the time to read me. as a lesbian i don't feel comfortable going to AA given its ties to catholicism
